Hi,

Thanks for reaching out — happy to clarify the difference between limit and market orders on Novig.

A **limit order** lets you set the **maximum price you’ll pay** (if buying) or the **minimum price you’ll accept** (if selling). Your order will only fill at your limit price or better. If there aren’t enough matching orders available at that price, it may fill partially or stay open until it’s matched (or until you cancel it).

A **market order** is designed to fill **as quickly as possible** at the best available prices currently in the order book. Because it prioritizes speed over price, the final fill price can vary depending on available liquidity and can be worse than what you expected if the market is moving or the order book is thin.

**When to use each:**
- Use a **limit order** when price matters most and you’re okay waiting (or not getting filled) to avoid unexpected pricing.
- Use a **market order** when getting filled quickly matters most and you’re comfortable with the fill occurring at the current available prices.

If you tell us which market you’re looking at and whether you’re trying to buy or sell, we can walk through an example with the prices you’re seeing.

Best,
Novig Support

Hi,

Thanks for reaching out—happy to clarify how order matching works on Novig.

In general, the order book matches orders based on price priority first (better prices get filled before worse prices). When multiple orders are at the same price, fills are typically handled by time priority (earlier orders at that price are filled before later ones).

If two orders are submitted at the exact same limit price at nearly the same time, the system uses the exchange’s recorded timestamp/sequence to determine which order arrived first. In practice, even very close submissions are ordered by the system, and the queue at that price level is processed in that sequence.

If you can share whether you’re placing orders on web or mobile (and the market you were watching), we can also point you to where you can see your order’s status (open/partially filled/filled) and position in the queue at a given price.

Best,
Novig Support
